/bin/bash -c "python3 - <<'PY'
import math
P = [[0.9, 0.1], [0.8, 0.2]]
nu = [8/9, 1/9]
xi = [sum(nu[i]*P[i][j] for i in range(2)) for j in range(2)]
Q = [[(nu[i]*P[i][j]+nu[j]*P[j][i])/(nu[i]+xi[i]) for j in range(2)] for i in range(2)]
Q2 = [[sum(Q[i][k]*Q[k][j] for k in range(2)) for j in range(2)] for i in range(2)]
def entropy(matrix):
    return -sum(x*math.log(x) for row in matrix for x in row if x)
print('nu =', nu)
print('xi =', xi)
print('P_nu =', Q)
print('P_nu squared =', Q2)
print('H(1) =', entropy(Q))
print('H(2) =', entropy(Q2))
print('unweighted squared row distance at t=1 =', sum((Q[0][j]-Q[1][j])**2 for j in range(2)))
print('diffusion distance squared at t=1 =', sum((Q[0][j]-Q[1][j])**2/nu[j] for j in range(2)))
PY"

strengths: Significance: Clustering weakly connected directed graphs is a useful problem. The proposed operator has a valid reversible-walk construction when P is stochastic and the vertex measure is positive. Table 3 reports promising gains on the chain and core-periphery DiSBMs and Political Blogs.

Originality: Combining degree-dependent vertex measures, power-iteration embeddings, random projections, and sampled entropy selection is a useful practical synthesis. The degree-heterogeneity experiments provide insight into settings where the proposed weighting helps.

Presentation and evaluation: The pipeline figure, Algorithm 1, and extensive parameter studies make the approach accessible. Reporting variability over 100 runs and giving PIC baselines the same projection and time-selection machinery are positive experimental choices.

Limitations and ethics: The manuscript acknowledges parameter sensitivity and problematic entropy behavior on some datasets. These disclosures are helpful. The benchmark-based algorithmic research presents no apparent material ethical concern.
weaknesses: Soundness—entropy guarantee: Proposition 3.5 is false even under favorable assumptions. Take P=[[0.9,0.1],[0.8,0.2]] and ν=(8/9,1/9). Equation 3 gives P_(ν)=P, which is irreducible, aperiodic, and reversible. Nevertheless, the stated entropy decreases from H(1)=0.825485 to H(2)=0.713440. Appendix E's Jensen step is invalid for a general row-stochastic matrix. This undermines the theoretical justification for time selection. Additionally, Equation 9 computes the ith column of P_(ν)^t, rather than its ith row, so the described sampled estimator does not implement Equation 7 as written.

Soundness—diffusion geometry: Definition 3.4 and Appendix E use P_(ν)=ΦΛΦᵀ for a generally nonsymmetric reversible matrix, omitting the stationary-distribution weighting. The proof also incorrectly invokes inverse-π orthogonality for eigenvectors declared orthonormal in ℓ²(π). More substantively, clustering unweighted rows of P_(ν)^t, or their isotropic random projections, does not preserve the inverse-π-weighted distance in Equation 4. The connection between the theoretical geometry and the implemented embedding needs correction.

Scalability: The headline O(N^(3/2)) complexity explicitly claimed for dense graphs is unsupported. The stated multiplication of an N×N operator by an N×√N embedding costs O(N^(5/2)) per iteration using conventional multiplication; the sparse cost is O(|E|√N). Time selection incurs additional work. Comparing against O(N³) full eigendecomposition also overlooks partial iterative eigensolvers. Figure 3 lacks the solver and hardware details needed to substantiate the claimed advantage.

Applicability and limitations: P=D_out^(-1)W is undefined at sinks, yet handling graphs with sinks is central to the motivation and evaluation. No dangling-node convention is specified; simply leaving zero rows makes Equation 3 substochastic at those vertices. Appendix D.2 also invokes strong connectivity of the original graph to explain entropy failures, although the proposed construction is intended to require only weak connectivity. These assumptions and implementation choices need a consistent treatment.

Evaluation and reproducibility: Appendix B.2 defines the reverse-edge branch of S using W_ij when its condition requires W_ij=0. Consequently, S is not Hermitian as written, raising uncertainty about the implemented Simple-Herm baseline. Code is only promised upon publication, and preprocessing, time-search limits, KNEEDLE settings, and eigensolver configurations are insufficiently specified. These omissions make it difficult to resolve whether the mathematical inconsistencies are transcription errors or affect the reported comparisons.

Evidence and presentation: Figure 7(e) places the selected entropy time on an approximately 0.6 AMI plateau, while earlier times achieve approximately 1.0. This contradicts the claim that entropy selection consistently matches or exceeds the alternatives and needs reconciliation with the 1.00 DiSBM C-P result in Table 3. Descriptions also alternate between increasing entropy, expected entropy decay, elbow selection, and entropy maximization. The reported gains are promising, but the reliability of the automatic selection procedure is not established.
